chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Muḥammad al-Ashʿarī, from Muʿallā ibn Muḥammad, from Abī al-Faḍl ʿAbdullāh ibn Idrīs, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, who said:
I was in the presence of Abī Jaʿfar al-Thānī عليه السلام, and I brought up the differing of the Shīʿah.

So he said: O Muḥammad, indeed Allah, Blessed and Exalted, never ceased being singular in His Oneness. Then He created Muḥammad, and ʿAlī, and Fāṭimah. Then they remained for a thousand dahr. Then He created all things, and made them witness their creation, and caused their obedience to be binding upon them, and delegated their affairs to them. So they make halal whatever they will, and make haram whatever they will; and they do not will except that Allah, Blessed and Exalted, wills.
Then he said: O Muḥammad, this is the religion such that whoever goes ahead of it slips away, whoever falls behind it is effaced, and whoever adheres to it joins it. Take it to yourself, O Muḥammad.

key_terms.أَلْفَ دَهْرٍ: A thousand ages or vast spans of time before the creation of all things.
key_terms.الدِّينَةُ: The religion or divinely ordained path referred to in the narration.
key_terms.طَاعَتَهُمْ: The obedience due to them by divine command.
key_terms.فَوَّضَ: He delegated or consigned authority over affairs.
key_terms.لَزِمَهَا: He adhered to it firmly and remained committed to it.
key_terms.يُحَرِّمُونَ: They declare forbidden by Allah’s granted authority.
key_terms.يُحِلُّونَ: They declare lawful by Allah’s granted authority.

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith from al-Kāfī say about the creation and authority of Muḥammad, ʿAlī, and Fāṭimah?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a theological and cosmological statement about the precedence of Muḥammad, ʿAlī, and Fāṭimah in creation and their divinely granted authority by Allah, Blessed and Exalted. It concludes by framing this teaching as the true religion: excess beyond it leads astray, falling short of it leads to loss, and firm adherence to it leads to salvation.
